questions.question: At what Reynolds number did the authors locate the onset of inertial corrections, and what length-scale comparison defines it?

options.A: Rec≈0.05, when l=a/Re becomes comparable to ξ0
options.B: Rec≈2.3, when ξ⊥ equals the particle diameter
options.C: Rec≈0.001, when the Stokes drag vanishes
options.D: Rec≈0.6, when the Schmidt number diverges

questions.rationale: The onset is set by the inertial screening length matching the Stokes sedimentation length.
questions.evidence_quote:
We ﬁnd that the onset of inertial corrections to Stokes
sedimentation occurs when the inertial screening length l = a/Re becomes similar to the Stokes
sedimentation length ξ0, at Rec = a/ξ0 ≈0.05. For Re > Rec, inertial screening signiﬁcantly
reduces both the magnitude and spatial extent of the particle velocity ﬂuctuations.

questions.question: How was Re defined for the measured suspension?

options.A: Va/η, with η the suspension viscosity
options.B: 2Va/ν, with V the particle velocity, a the radius, and ν the fluid kinematic viscosity
options.D: aV/ν, with V the isolated-sphere terminal speed

questions.rationale: The manuscript defines Reynolds number from particle velocity and radius.
questions.evidence_quote:
Re ≡2V a/ν (V is
the particle velocity, a the radius, and ν the ﬂuid kinematic viscosity).

questions.question: What particle and suspension conditions were used across the principal experiment?

options.A: Polymer spheres radius 13.7 μm at φ=0.6
options.B: Glass beads radius 137 μm at φ=0.6
options.C: Glass beads radius 137±9 μm at volume fraction φ=0.06
options.D: Brownian spheres radius 1.37 mm at φ=0.06

questions.rationale: The reported beads were monodisperse glass of radius 137±9 μm, and φ was fixed at 0.06.
questions.evidence_quote:
The particles used in our experiments were monodisperse glass beads of radius a = 137±9
µm. They were dispersed in various mixtures of glycerol and water, enabling us to examine
the very low to moderate Reynolds number regimes, 0.001 ≤Re ≤2.3. In all cases the
volume fraction is φ = 0.06.

questions.question: What empirical expression did the authors use to fit the longitudinal correlation length over Reynolds number?
questions.rationale: Equation (1) gives the stated fourth-root fit.

questions.question: Which feature of the perpendicular velocity correlation changed in the inertial sample at Re=2.3?

options.A: The long-range negative dip in Cz(x) disappeared
options.C: Its decay length grew beyond ξ
options.D: It developed a second positive maximum

questions.rationale: The paper highlights loss of the negative transverse correlation dip.
questions.evidence_quote: the long-range negative correlation dip in Cz(x) is completely absent

questions.question: In the modified Hinch model, what is the Reynolds number appropriate to drag acting on a correlated region of size ξ?
questions.rationale: The force balance treats a correlated region of scale ξ, so its Reynolds number uses ξ.

questions.question: In the modified Hinch force balance, how is the inertial part of the drag coefficient parameterized?
questions.rationale: The paper uses an empirical inertial drag correction valid to moderate Reynolds numbers.
questions.evidence_quote: The term βRe ≈0.133Re0.78 is the inertial part

questions.question: Why did omitting inertial drag corrections from the modified Hinch model substantially underpredict the observed suppression of fluctuations?

options.A: It removed the buoyancy force and predicted zero fluctuations
options.B: It assumed a constant particle volume fraction
options.C: It increased the modeled correlation length with Re
options.D: It left only the modest effect of shrinking ξ and omitted the increasing drag term

questions.rationale: Without drag correction the model included only the reduction in ξ, which was insufficient.
questions.evidence_quote: greatly underestimates the observed drop in ﬂuctuation magnitudes

questions.question: Why did the authors reinterpret Cowan et al.'s reported Re0≈0.3 samples as showing no contradiction to inertial screening?

options.A: The concentration-adjusted Reynolds numbers were estimated at or below Rec in all samples
options.B: The original experiment used Brownian particles outside the non-Brownian regime
options.C: Their correlation lengths were measured only at Re>2.3
options.D: The critical threshold depends on cell width rather than ξ0

questions.rationale: The authors estimate the true Re using concentration-specific V and η, placing the samples below onset.
questions.evidence_quote:
They compared many concentrations 0.19 ≤φ ≤0.5, at
both Re0 = 0.007 and Re0 = 0.3, and concluded that, contrary to expectations, the velocity
ﬂuctuations were independent of Reynolds number for Re < 1. We ﬁrst note that they
deﬁned Re0 ≡2aV0/η0 based upon the inﬁnite dilution values V0 and η0, not the values at
the high concentrations studied. Using our deﬁnition Re = 2aV/η, we estimate that the
Re0 = 0.3 samples range from 0.001 <∼Re <∼0.05. Our critical Reynolds number for the
appearance of inertial inﬂuence, Rec = a/ξ0, can also be evaluated from their ﬁndings that
ξ ∼11aφ−1/3, resulting in Rec ≈0.06. We therefore ﬁnd that Re <∼Rec for all of their
samples, consistent with their ﬁndings of no inertial eﬀects..

questions.question: What physical assumption does the successful Hinch-model comparison support even when inertia is present?

options.A: Velocity correlations become infinite-ranged at moderate Re
options.B: A random particle density distribution remains a useful underlying assumption
options.C: Particles settle independently without concentration fluctuations
options.D: The Stokes drag law remains exact at all measured Reynolds numbers

questions.rationale: The conclusion explicitly says model success suggests its random-density assumption remains valid.
questions.evidence_quote: assumption of a random particle density distribution remains valid in the presence of inertia.
